steps.title: Load a valley
steps.say: An invented valley: 120 by 80 cells of ten metres, hills, a stream and four old field terraces. A LiDAR ground model is already registered, and one trench has been laid out but not dug. Somewhere under the ground is a walled enclosure with buildings and a road; the generator knows where, and says so only at the end.

steps.title: Register the multispectral survey
steps.say: A vegetation index from satellite imagery, 9,600 cells, registered against the site and checked for shape and range.

steps.title: Each survey on its own
steps.say: LiDAR: residual relief against a smoothed surface, averaged along short lines, steep ground masked. The terraces show up as strongly as the walls, and so does noise. The index: crop marks where the crop is stressed, only judged where there are crops. The hidden truth says how each survey did alone.

steps.title: Fuse the evidence into candidate areas
steps.say: Per cell: prior odds of masonry times each survey's likelihood ratio, so a weak ridge and a weak crop mark in the same place add up and a strong ridge with no crop mark (a terrace) does not. Connected cells above the threshold are ranked, each with its evidence.

steps.title: Dig the trench
steps.say: Trench TR1 across the east side of the top candidate: six contexts from ploughsoil to natural, including a mortared limestone wall two courses high, and seven finds with their dates. Every record carries who entered it and when, and the stratigraphic sequence becomes edges in the knowledge graph.

contexts.description: mortared limestone wall, two courses surviving, 0.9 m wide
rubble collapse against the wall's east face

steps.title: Two reconstructions of the same evidence
steps.say: The enclosure reading closes the best-supported rectangle and calls the lines inside it buildings; the field reading keeps the lines as boundaries and extends nothing. From the surveys alone they are close. The trench found a wall where the enclosure reading drew one, and the confidences move.

steps.title: Click a wall
steps.say: The east wall: its cells, each survey's contribution, the posterior, the zones, the trench across it with its contexts and finds, and a date after which it was built. Then the north wall, which is mostly drawn rather than seen, and says so.

steps.title: The graph, the boxes, the audit trail
steps.say: Everything recorded is a node or an edge: site, surveys, zones, trench, contexts, finds, hypotheses. The walls as boxes for a viewer to draw. And the log that cannot be edited.
